It derives complete leading and subleading splitting functions for all Standard Model particles, establishes a matching dictionary between massless and massive couplings, and provides a recursive bootstrap for higher-point functions, extending naturally to EFT operators and higher orders.
AI.motivation: While on-shell spinor-helicity methods work well for massless QCD splitting functions, a systematic on-shell construction for massive particles incorporating finite-mass effects is underdeveloped. This work aims to fill that gap.
AI.method: The formalism uses Soper-Weinberg collinear spinors derived from a light-front Galilean subgroup of the Poincaré group. Massive momenta and spinors are decomposed relative to fixed lightlike vectors n and n̄, making the m < p_T ≪ p_+ expansion manifest. Leading-order structures are matched to massless 3-point amplitudes; subleading components are probed via an additional Higgs momentum along n̄, linking to massless 4-point amplitudes. Higher-point splitting functions are obtained via a recursive bootstrap with a universal substitution rule from Galilean symmetry.
AI.result: The complete set of leading and subleading massive splitting functions for all Standard Model particles is derived. A systematic matching dictionary between massless and massive coupling coefficients at 3- and 4-point levels is established.
AI.conclusion: The framework extends naturally to EFT operators and higher perturbative orders, providing a flexible computational tool for precision collider physics and parton shower development.

title: Type I/II Vortex Dynamics With Excited Normal Modes
summary: We investigate the effects of excited normal modes on vortex dynamics in the Abelian Higgs model in the type I (static attraction) and type II (static repulsion) regimes. We demonstrate that shape normal modes compete with the static inter-vortex forces. This can result in excited type I (II) vortices repelling (attracting). In addition we observe the existence of spectral walls that prevent the formation (break up) of bound states in type I (II) systems. We study the long lived quasi-bound states and orbits induced by their competing forces and the effective centrifugal forces. Finally, we observe that the effect is strong enough to induce vortex-antivortex pairs to follow long-lived orbits.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how excited shape normal modes affect vortex dynamics in the Abelian Higgs model, showing that these modes can reverse the static inter-vortex forces (type I vortices repel, type II attract), create spectral walls blocking bound state formation/breakup, and induce long-lived quasi-bound states and vortex-antivortex orbits.
AI.motivation: To understand how excited normal modes alter the static interaction forces between vortices in the Abelian Higgs model, potentially reversing attraction/repulsion behaviors and creating new dynamical phenomena.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical study of the Abelian Higgs model in both type I (static attraction) and type II (static repulsion) regimes, examining the competition between shape normal modes and static inter-vortex forces.
AI.result: Excited shape normal modes can reverse the static force direction (type I vortices repel, type II attract). Spectral walls prevent bound state formation/breakup. Long-lived quasi-bound states and orbits emerge from competing forces and effective centrifugal effects, including vortex-antivortex pair orbits.
AI.conclusion: Shape mode excitations significantly impact vortex dynamics, introducing competing dynamical forces strong enough to induce long-lived orbital motion even in vortex-antivortex pairs, which has implications for understanding non-equilibrium vortex phenomena.

title: Next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to pion (kaon)-induced exclusive Drell-Yan process
summary: The high-energy pion and kaon beams proposed for future experiments at J-PARC offer a unique opportunity to investigate exclusive Drell-Yan processes induced by pions or kaons, which correspond to inverse deeply virtual meson production with $M=π,K$. To facilitate precise comparisons between theoretical predictions and forthcoming experimental data, we calculate the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD corrections to the processes $π^- p\to γ^*(\to l^+l^-) + n$ and $K^- p\to γ^*(\to l^+l^-) + Λ$. Our calculations are performed within the generalized parton distribution (GPD) factorization framework, accurate to leading twist in the generalized Bjorken limit ($Q^2\gg |t|,\,Λ_{\rm QCD}^2$). We find that the NNLO QCD corrections are substantial and positive; therefore, their inclusion is imperative for reliable theoretical predictions in confrontation with future experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents NNLO QCD corrections for exclusive Drell-Yan processes induced by pion and kaon beams at J-PARC, finding substantial positive corrections essential for reliable theoretical predictions.
AI.motivation: Future J-PARC experiments with high-energy pion and kaon beams enable exclusive Drell-Yan processes (inverse deeply virtual meson production). Precise theoretical predictions are needed for comparison with upcoming experimental data, requiring higher-order QCD corrections.
AI.method: NNLO QCD corrections are calculated within the GPD factorization framework at leading twist in the generalized Bjorken limit (Q² ≫ |t|, Λ²_QCD) for π⁻p → γ*(→ℓ⁺ℓ⁻) + n and K⁻p → γ*(→ℓ⁺ℓ⁻) + Λ processes.
AI.result: The NNLO QCD corrections are substantial and positive in sign.
AI.conclusion: Inclusion of NNLO corrections is imperative for reliable theoretical predictions to confront future experimental data at J-PARC.

title: Magnetic corrections to the fermionic Casimir effect with Lorentz symmetry violation and a compactified extra dimension
summary: In this work I study the effect of a magnetic field on the Casimir effect due to a massive, charged fermion field that violates Lorentz invariance in an aether-like manner while maintaining CPT, in a space with one toroidally compactified extra dimension. I take the fermion field to obey MIT bag boundary conditions on two identical square parallel plates. I do this investigation using the zeta function technique that enables me to calculate the Casimir energy and pressure in the presence of a constant magnetic field perpendicular to the plates. I examine the cases of timelike Lorentz violation, of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction of the magnetic field, of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field, and of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction of the compactified extra dimension. In all scenarios, I find simple and accurate analytic expressions of the magnetic field dependent Casimir energy and pressure.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the Casimir effect for a massive, charged fermion field with Lorentz violation (aether-like, CPT-preserving) in a space with one toroidally compactified extra dimension, under a constant magnetic field perpendicular to parallel plates with MIT bag boundary conditions, using the zeta function technique to derive analytic expressions for Casimir energy and pressure for various Lorentz violation scenarios.
AI.motivation: To understand how Lorentz-violating effects (in an aether-like CPT-preserving framework) and a magnetic field jointly influence the Casimir effect for massive charged fermions in a spacetime with an extra compactified dimension, extending previous studies to more complex field configurations.
AI.method: Zeta function regularization technique is used to compute Casimir energy and pressure for a massive charged fermion field with Lorentz violation, under a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with MIT bag boundary conditions on two parallel plates, in a space with one toroidally compactified extra dimension.
AI.result: Simple and accurate analytic expressions for the magnetic field-dependent Casimir energy and pressure are obtained for four scenarios: timelike Lorentz violation, spacelike Lorentz violation along the magnetic field direction, spacelike Lorentz violation perpendicular to the magnetic field, and spacelike Lorentz violation along the compactified extra dimension.
AI.conclusion: The Casimir effect for massive charged fermions with Lorentz violation and a magnetic field can be analytically characterized in all considered Lorentz violation scenarios, providing a framework for testing Lorentz symmetry violations via Casimir measurements in compactified extra-dimensional settings.

title: Particle production from bubble collisions
summary: Collisions of ultra-relativistic bubbles during cosmological phase transitions can produce particles much heavier than the transition scale. Previous analyses modelled this process as the off-shell decay of the scalar background. We show that its results parametrically overestimate hard particle production and depend on the gauge choice and the coordinate choice in field space. We propose an alternative formalism, analogous to the partonic description of high-energy collisions. In the ultra-relativistic limit, the colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among the quanta constituting the Lorentz-contracted walls. We apply this approach to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particle production, and study the implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production and primordial gravitational waves.

AI.tldr: This paper critiques previous methods for modeling particle production from ultra-relativistic bubble collisions during phase transitions, showing they overestimate production and are gauge-dependent. It proposes a new partonic-like formalism where hard production comes from on-shell scatterings of quanta in Lorentz-contracted bubble walls, and applies this to dark matter, leptogenesis, and gravitational waves.
AI.motivation: Previous analyses of particle production from ultra-relativistic bubble collisions during cosmological phase transitions have parametric overestimates and suffer from gauge and coordinate choice dependencies, necessitating a more accurate formalism.
AI.method: The authors propose a partonic description analogous to high-energy collisions, where colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard particle production arises from on-shell scatterings among quanta in the Lorentz-contracted walls, applied to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particles.
AI.result: Previous off-shell decay models parametrically overestimate hard particle production and are gauge/coordinate dependent; the new on-shell scattering formalism provides more reliable production rates.
AI.conclusion: The new partonic formalism resolves prior inaccuracies and has implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production, and primordial gravitational waves from cosmological phase transitions.

title: Analytical and Numerical Study of Quartic Nonlinear Electrodynamics in Holographic Fermion Systems
summary: We study how the leading string-inspired quartic correction $α'^2 F^4$ modifies holographic fermionic observables in a bottom-up $AdS_4/CFT_3$ model. The gauge sector is described by Maxwell electrodynamics supplemented by the quartic interaction, while the geometry is kept fixed in the probe approximation. We first analyze the nonlinear electrostatic background and derive an exact first integral of the gauge equation, the associated constitutive relation for the radial electric field, the critical coupling for globally regular solutions, and weak-coupling expansions for the electrostatic potential and chemical potential. We then use these backgrounds to compute the retarded Green's function and spectral function of charged probe fermions. The quartic interaction increases the chemical potential, lowers the effective ratio $T/μ$, shifts the Fermi momentum, and enhances the spectral weight without destroying the holographic Fermi surface. We further show that the fermionic observables inherit the even-power dependence on $α'$ implied by the analytic structure of the gauge sector. The resulting probe-limit analysis makes explicit how quartic bulk nonlinearities propagate from the bulk to boundary fermionic observables.

The quartic term increases chemical potential, lowers T/μ, shifts Fermi momentum, and enhances spectral weight while preserving the Fermi surface. Fermionic observables show even-power dependence on α'.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher-derivative corrections from string theory (specifically the leading quartic F⁴ term) affect holographic fermionic observables, bridging string-inspired corrections to boundary fermionic behavior in a controlled bottom-up AdS/CFT setup.
AI.method: A bottom-up AdS₄/CFT₃ holographic model where Maxwell electrodynamics is supplemented by a quartic F⁴ interaction, with fixed AdS geometry in the probe limit. The authors derive exact first integrals, analyze electrostatic backgrounds, and compute retarded Green's functions and spectral functions for probe fermions.

Fermionic observables exhibit even-power dependence on α', inherited from the gauge sector's analytic structure.
AI.conclusion: Quartic bulk nonlinearities propagate in a controlled way to boundary fermionic observables, and the probe-limit analysis explicitly demonstrates how such corrections modify fermionic behavior in holographic models.

title: New exact bispectrum shapes in multifield inflation
summary: Using the effective field theory of multiple inflationary fluctuations, we present the first analytical calculation of the primordial bispectrum in which the quadratic mixing between curvature and isocurvature fluctuations is treated non-perturbatively. Building upon the operator representation of the exact linear solutions proposed in Ref.~\cite{Huenupi:2026abj}, we derive a simpler integral representation for these mixed mode functions. We prove that all scale-invariant tree-level bispectra reduce to a single vertex diagram, which can be evaluated with a Schwinger-parameter integral over independent pre-computable leg kernels. We showcase the power of our approach by considering the cubic time-derivative interaction $\dot{\pic}^3$, which leads to a purely single-field, equilateral phenomenology at small mixing. On the contrary, at strong mixing the obtained bispectrum shapes decorrelate from the equilateral template and become genuinely multifield, with a large amplitude, motivating a dedicated data analysis. The squeezed limit is obtained analytically in a closed form at any dimensionless mixing strength $\la$ for an isocurvature field of bare mass $m$ and features a cosmological collider signal set by $ν_{\rm eff} = i \muf=\sqrt{9/4-m^2/H^2-\la^2}$, with an effective mass dressed by $\la$, as previously evidenced in numerical or semi-analytical calculations. Our results encompass the $\la \ll 1$ limit of usual perturbative calculations, where the amplitude of the signal is necessarily small, but they also surpass them, thus opening a new analytical window into large multifield primordial non-Gaussianities.

The authors derive a simpler integral representation for mixed mode functions, show that all scale-invariant tree-level bispectra reduce to a single vertex diagram evaluable via Schwinger-parameter integrals, and demonstrate that strong mixing yields genuinely multifield bispectrum shapes decorrelated from equilateral templates, with a cosmological collider signal characterized by an effective mass dressed by the mixing strength.
AI.motivation: Standard perturbative calculations of multifield inflation bispectra are limited to weak mixing (λ ≪ 1) and produce small non-Gaussianities. A fully analytical framework capable of handling strong quadratic mixing between curvature and isocurvature fluctuations non-perturbatively has been lacking, which is needed to access potentially large multifield primordial non-Gaussianities.

They prove that scale-invariant tree-level bispectra reduce to a single vertex diagram evaluated via a Schwinger-parameter integral over independent pre-computable leg kernels.

title: Relativistic time-commutative dynamics with $κ$-plane noncommutativity
summary: In the last decades, spacetime noncommutativity and the associated deformations of relativistic symmetries have attracted a lot of interest, as several phenomenological windows into quantum gravity are approaching genuine Planck-scale sensitivity. From time to time it has been suggested that valuable insight into these conceptual challenges could come from the analysis of appropriately designed first-quantized toy models, in which major technical and interpretive issues can be effectively managed or sidestepped altogether.
